nodes_add.name: Nitya Tripta (S. Balakrishna Pillai)
nodes_add.note: Student of Atmananda who kept notes of his talks 1950-1959, published 1963.

nodes_add.name: K. Padmanabha Menon (Sri Adwayananda)
nodes_add.note: Atmananda's eldest son; taught at Anandawadi until 2001; compiled Atmananda Tattwa Samhita (1973) from tape recordings.

nodes_add.name: Hari Gopalan Citar
nodes_add.note: Disciple to whom followers say the Akilathirattu Ammanai was dictated; spelled Arigopalan Citar in some Wikipedia passages.

edges_upsert.note: Eldest son; continued the teaching at Anandawadi until 2001 (Wikipedia).
Followers say the Akilam was dictated to him; dictation date given as 1840 or 1841 on Wikipedia.

glossary.def: Pali for loving-kindness, a Buddhist meditation of wishing wellbeing first to oneself, then to others.
Existence, consciousness and bliss, the traditional description of Brahman. Atmananda rendered the last term as peace.
In Ayyavazhi, one of the chief disciples of Vaikundar, named after the Pandava brothers.
The daily service or worship performed at Ayyavazhi shrines.
Name for groups in Bengal who read the love of Radha and Krishna in a bodily, erotic way; criticised by Bhaktivinoda and Bhaktisiddhanta.
Training in which a person watches a measurement of a body process, such as skin temperature or brain waves, to learn to influence it.
Alternate nostril breathing, taught to balance the breath and calm the nervous system.

issues: dipa-ma: daughter's birth year (Wikipedia 1950) and the details of her death (bowing before a Buddha statue) rest on Wikipedia and Encyclopedia.com; both flagged by Wikipedia as needing citations.
atmananda-krishna-menon: accounts of his realization in 1923 come from student-run sites; the horse-carriage anecdote is as summarised from Renard part one.
ayya-vaikundar: Wikipedia articles disagree on the names of the Seedars and on the penance chronology; the Akilam print date is 1927 or 1933.
chinmayananda: mission site dates the Rishikesh visit to September 1947, a Wikipedia mirror to summer 1947; quotes of the Tapovan tribute come from the mission archive.
bhaktisiddhanta: ages at memorising the Gita (seven or nine) and age at death (62 or 63) differ across sources; Gaura Kishora's initiation date 1900 or 1901.
bhaktivinoda: Wikipedia and devotional chronologies differ on marriage year, cholera year and Hindu College enrolment.

swami-rama: Darbhanga degree dated 1945 (Encyclopedia.com) or 1960 (Hospital Trust); the sealed cave, London, Moscow, Japan claims rest on the Trust alone; the Tigunait biography is titled At the Eleventh Hour (2001) in the chapter, while Encyclopedia.com lists Swami Rama of the Himalayas (1999).
